inputs.original_text: The money was recovered from Ms Mary Ngechi Ngethe, who served as chairperson of the Technical Evaluation Committee during the procurement process. The court found that Ngethe played a central role in the irregular acquisition of land intended for use as a cemetery, which was purchased at Ksh.283 million despite being unsuitable.
inputs.modified_text: This case with Ms Mary Ngechi Ngethe, who chaired the Technical Evaluation Committee, lays bare the systemic institutional failures that let those in power squander public resources, wasting Ksh.283 million on an unsuitable site for a cemetery that communities desperately need. While the court's order to recover the full amount from her offers a sliver of accountability, it underscores how these structures are built to serve elite interests over the basic needs of working families and marginalized groups. Abuses like this deepen inequality by stealing resources meant for vulnerable populations, and they make it urgent that we push for real structural reforms to transform institutions so they protect the public instead of shielding corruption at every level.
